content.body:
Firing a tungsten-core AP round, the SA.mle.37L/53 (the "Samel 37") was the most powerful purpose-built anti-tank gun in the world until the advent of the PaK.40. It could penetrate any German armor at long range, and the Germans learned to respect it. Its development was in fact so secret that it wasn't even distributed to units until Sept.1939 with the outbreak of war imminent. Unfortunately, there was no HE round developed for it so it is unsuitable for fighting infantry or even light vehicle targets ... the terrific penetration of the AP round means that even at moderate ranges it can pass entirely through a light truck or even some armored cars, doing little damage.
The French 47mm heavy AT gun is an exceptionally good gun and will outrage, outshoot, and outclass pretty much anything except the later AT guns in the over 50mm class. Its easily towed, the low center of gravity making it behave particularly well behind a truck. Deployed, the gun sits low between the wheels, yet has a decent arc of fire.
The sights are adjustable, but the dispersion is a little troublesome ... expect to have to put a few rounds downrange to hit targets at 1km or more. Moreover (and probably the flip side of the quickly manhandled feature) the carriage is pretty light for a very high-powered round, and so it jumps around a bit, it take some time to reacquire targets. Because of this, it's strongly recommended to use the range-setting whenever possible ... its hard enough to reset the gun centerline on target without having to remember how much you had adjusted for range last time.
Feel free to engage any German tanks at 1000m or less, although it's probably worth it to hesitate as long as possible before hitting a Tiger or a StuG, just on general principles, and certainly avoid the frontal aspect shot as these types of German tanks are heavily armoured on their frontal hull and turret facings.
